parameters.content:
# Classify company descriptions with Apify
Turn descriptions you already have into labels for lead segmentation. Supply your own categories; this workflow does not scrape websites or find contacts.

## Before you start
Use an Apify account and n8n. The workflow is free; Actor usage follows its published pricing. Read the [setup and recovery guide](https://github.com/CHYYX/Bridge-ai/blob/lanseq-apify-n8n-20261115/examples/apify-company-classification/README.md).

**Validation:** orchestration checked on n8n 2.47.7 with mock responses. Live end-to-end execution and classification accuracy are not established.

# Setup checklist
1. In **Input and budget**, replace the synthetic records and labels. Each record needs a unique `id` and a `text` description.
2. Select your existing Apify **HTTP Header Auth** credential on **Start Actor once**, **Read run**, and **Read results**. Keep secrets in n8n credentials, never in this JSON.
3. Review build `0.1.3`, current Actor pricing, and caps: **$0.05/run; $0.10 total**. Caps are spending limits, not estimates.
4. Set `executeModelCalls: true` only when ready, then run manually.

Text goes to Apify and Lanseq. Execution history may retain input; use data you have permission to process.

## 1. Prepare the batch plan
**Edit Input and budget before running.** Choose labels that match your business task.

Validation rejects duplicate IDs and oversized input before any HTTP call: IDs ≤100 UTF-8 bytes, text ≤8,000 bytes, ≤20 labels and ≤10 fields.

The plan splits records into batches of **up to 20**, with one remote run at a time. Keep the original IDs to join results back to your source.

## 2. Create one Actor run
Start the current batch and remember the returned run and Dataset IDs.

**No automatic POST retry.** If the request times out, check Apify Runs before submitting again: it may already have started and incurred charges.

Never blindly replay an uncertain submission.

## 3. Poll without restarting
Read the saved run every **10 seconds** until it finishes, fails or reaches the five-minute polling deadline.

The Wait node returns to Poll context, not to Start Actor once. Polling timeout **does not cancel** the remote run.

Check Apify Runs before recovery. A terminal status is not proof that every input produced a valid result.

## 4. Inspect the final report
Read the Dataset and match rows by original ID. Continue only if the batch is complete and structurally valid.

Missing, duplicate, unexpected or failed rows stop later submissions. **Final report** retains earlier results and marks missing and unsubmitted records.

Review these flags before writing to a CRM or Sheet. Structural validation is not semantic accuracy; check labels against known answers.
